hints.content: In order to find $G'(1)$, we should first find an expression for $G'(x)$ (for any input $x$) in terms of $f$, $g$, and their derivatives.

So $G'(x)=\dfrac{f'(x)g(x)-f(x)g'(x)}{[g(x)]^2}$.

We can now plug $x=1$ into this expression and evaluate. Here is the table of values again, for your convenience:

$x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | $f'(x)$ | $g'(x)$
:-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-:
$1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $5$ | $-6$

Let's plug in those values!

$\begin{align}
G'(1)&=\dfrac{f'(1)g(1)-f(1)g'(1)}{[g(1)]^2}
\\\\
&=\dfrac{(5)(3)-(2)(-6)}{(3)^2}
\\\\
&=\dfrac{27}{9}
\\\\
&=3
\end{align}$
